newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia says meeting with Taiwan envoy personal.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia says meeting with Taiwan envoy personal.

text.p: Malaysian Foreign Minister Abdullah Ahmad Badawi said on Friday a recent meeting with his Taiwanese counterpart was personal and not official and would not affect Malaysia's support of the "one China" policy.

Malaysia would continue with the "one China" policy which recognises only the People's Republic of China (PRC) as the legitimate government for all of China including Taiwan, the national Bernama news agency quoted him as saying.
But at the same time, Malaysia planned to continue the existing economic and trade relations between Kuala Lumpur and Taipei, Abdullah said.

"Malaysia practises the one China policy and has no intention at any time to review the policy...we are firm on the one China stand but our relationship with Taiwan is one of trade and investment and Taiwan has had economic relations with us for a long time," he said.

The unannounced visit by Taiwanese Foreign Minister John Chang last Friday to Malaysia prompted an angry response from China, which views Taiwan as a renegade province not entitled to any international contacts.
China said on Tuesday it had asked Malaysia to clarify the visit by Chang.
Abdullah said Taiwan was one of the four countries with the most active trade and investment relations with Malaysia and one of its biggest investors.
"So we cannot ignore Taiwan which plays an active role in trade and investment in this country," he said.

"So whatever contact with its leaders is made on an unofficial and personal basis, it cannot and should not be regarded as affecting our relations with the PRC or as an intention to change the one China policy." he added.
According to latest figures, Taiwan was the second largest investor in Malaysia, after Japan, at 1.44 billion ringgit ($576 million) or 19.56 per cent of the total foreign investments in the country.
About 900 Taiwanese companies are operating in Malaysia.
